title: What I've been watching
takeaway: Look around honestly. Injustice can't last, and the blood of the innocent is never wasted.
scene: Every couplet ends with 'vekh rehaan', which means 'I keep watching'. The poet is a witness. He describes what he sees in his country and his time, and much of it is painful.

original: میں زندگی دی شہ رگ اتے چل دے آرے ویکھ رہیاں
الفت دی راہاں تے ڈگے ہمت ہارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Main zindagi di shah-rag utte chalde aare vekh rehaan
Ulfat di raahaan te digge himmat haare vekh rehaan
translation: I keep watching saws cutting across the jugular vein of life;
I keep watching people fallen on the roads of love, having lost heart.
couplets.story: He sees life itself under attack, as if a saw were running across its throat. He also sees people who set out to love and fell by the roadside, having given up.

original: کجھ ایسے نے جنہاں نوں اپنی منزل دا راہ لبھدا نئیں
کجھ منزل پا کے بھل جاندے کرماں دے مارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Kujh aise ne jinhaan nu apni manzil da raah labhda nahin
Kujh manzil paa ke bhul jaande, karmaan de maare vekh rehaan
translation: There are some who can't find the road to their destination,
and some unlucky ones who reach it and then forget it; I keep watching.
couplets.story: Some people never find their way. Others actually get where they wanted to go, and then forget why they went. He watches both, and it's sad.

original: جیون دی رات ہنیری وچ فریاد کسے دی آئی اے
شبنم گلابی گلاں دی پلکاں تے تارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Jeevan di raat hanairi vich faryaad kise di aayi ae
Shabnam gulaabi gallaan di, palkaan te taare vekh rehaan
translation: In the dark night of life, someone's cry for help has come.
I keep watching dew on rosy cheeks, and stars on eyelashes.
couplets.story: In the darkness he hears someone calling for help. He sees tears on someone's cheeks like dewdrops, and hanging on their eyelashes like stars.

original: پھڑ کچا گھڑا الا نال صدق دے ٹھل جاندے وچ دریاواں دے
کجھ کنڈے بہہ کے تکدے نے ایہہ شوخ نظارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Phar kachcha ghara ala naal sidq de thal jaande vich dariyaavaan de
Kujh kande beh ke takde ne, eh shokh nazaare vekh rehaan
translation: Some grab an unbaked pot and set off sincerely into the rivers,
and some just sit on the bank and stare. I keep watching these bold scenes.
couplets.story: Like Sohni, some brave people grab a fragile pot and swim into the river with real faith. Others sit on the riverbank and just watch. He sees both kinds of people.

original: تہذیب ہے اج دے لوکاں دی ہے سستا خون انساناں دا
جس پاسے نظر اٹھاناواں میں خون دے دھارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Tehzeeb hai ajj de lokaan di, hai sasta khoon insaanaan da
Jis paase nazar uthaanaa vaan main khoon de dhaare vekh rehaan
translation: This is the 'civilisation' of today's people: human blood is cheap.
Wherever I raise my eyes, I keep watching streams of blood.
couplets.story: He says bitterly that today's so-called civilised people treat human life as cheap. Everywhere he looks, he sees bloodshed.

original: ایہہ یارو ضائع نئیں جانا جو ڈلھیا خون شہیداں دا
میں ظلم ستم دے ڈگدے ہوئے سب محل منارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Eh yaaro zaaya nahin jaana, jo dulhiya khoon shaheedaan da
Main zulm sitam de digde hoe sab mehal manaare vekh rehaan
translation: Friends, the blood the martyrs spilled will not go to waste.
I can already see the palaces and towers of tyranny falling.
couplets.story: But he holds on to hope. The blood of people who died for what's right won't be wasted. He can already see the great buildings of cruelty starting to crumble.

original: اے باغ دے مالی ہوش کریں اینان دی نیت نیک نئیں
ہر پھل دی پتی دے اتے میں شوخ شرارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Ae baagh de maali hosh kareen, inaan di neeyat nek nahin
Har phull di patti de utte main shokh sharaare vekh rehaan
translation: O gardener of this garden, wake up: these people don't mean well.
On every petal of every flower I see wild sparks.
couplets.story: He warns the 'gardener', whoever is meant to look after the country. Wake up. The people around you mean harm. Sparks are already landing on every flower, and the whole garden could catch fire.

original: اوجیہڑے بیٹھ چٹاناں تے ہر شے دا مونہہ چڑاندے سن
اج ڈبن لگے تیلیاں دے پئے لین سہارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: O jehre baith chataanaan te har shai da moonh chiraande san
Ajj dubban lagge teeliyaan de pae lain sahaare vekh rehaan
translation: Those who once sat on solid rock and mocked everything,
I now watch them drowning and clutching at straws.
couplets.story: The people who used to sit safe and proud, laughing at everyone, are now drowning. He watches them grab at tiny straws to stay afloat.

original: میں جیون دی پگڈنڈیاں تے راہ بھلے راہی ویکھے نیں
کجھ تھکے ہارے بیٹھے نیں کجھ پیر پسارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Main jeevan di pagdandiyaan te raah bhulle raahi vekhe nain
Kujh thakke haare baithe nain, kujh pair pasaare vekh rehaan
translation: On the narrow footpaths of life I've seen travellers who lost their way;
some sit worn out and defeated, some I watch stretched out for good.
couplets.story: On life's narrow paths, he has seen many people get lost. Some sat down, exhausted and beaten. Others lay down and never got up again.

original: ایس عشق دی راہ تے اے احمدؔ توں سنبھل سنبھل کے پیر دھریں
ایتھے ڈنگن خاطر ناگ کئی پئے لین ہلارے ویکھ رہیاں
transliteration: Is ishq di raah te ae Ahmad toon sambhal sambhal ke pair dhareen
Ethe dangan khaatir naag kayi pae lain hulaare vekh rehaan
translation: On this road of love, Ahmad, place your feet very carefully:
I can see many snakes swaying here, ready to strike.
couplets.story: He gives himself a warning. Walk very carefully on the road of love, Ahmad. He can see snakes swaying back and forth, ready to bite.

deeper:
The jugular vein (shah-rag) in the first line carries an echo of the Qur'an, where God is 'closer than the jugular vein' (50:16). Cutting at it is cutting at what is most precious and nearest to God. 'The blood of the martyrs will not go to waste' reflects the belief that God sees every injustice, and that tyranny eventually falls. This is mostly a poem of conscience: faith that speaks up about society.

The refrain 'I keep watching' matters too. The poet is a witness: he sees clearly and refuses to look away. Some travellers 'reach the destination and then forget it'. That is a sharp spiritual warning: arriving isn't enough if you fall asleep again.
why: It's a poem about paying attention: seeing what's really happening around you and not looking away.
prompt: What's something happening in the world right now that you think people should 'keep watching'?
